legend: Let rad(n)$$$(n)$$$ denote the product of all distinct prime divisors of the number n$$$n$$$. For example, rad(504)$$$(504)$$$ = rad(23⋅32⋅7)$$$(2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 7)$$$ =2⋅3⋅7$$$= 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7$$$ =42$$$=42$$$. We define rad(1)=1$$$(1) = 1$$$.

The statement of this problem is simple: you have an array a$$$a$$$ of size n$$$n$$$. You are given q$$$q$$$ queries [ℓ;r]$$$[\ell;r]$$$, and you need to compute rad of the product of the numbers aℓ,aℓ+1,…,ar$$$a_\ell, a_{\ell + 1}, \dots, a_r$$$, that is: rad(r∏i=ℓai)=rad(aℓ×aℓ+1×⋯×ar)$$\displaystyle\texttt{rad}\left(\prod_{i=\ell}^{r} a_i\right) = \texttt{rad}\left(a_\ell \times a_{\ell + 1} \times \dots \times a_r \right)$$ Since this number can be quite large, output it modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.

The second line of input contains n$$$n$$$ numbers ai$$$a_i$$$ (1≤ai≤2⋅105$$$1 \le a_i \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$), the array a$$$a$$$.
In the following q$$$q$$$ lines, two numbers ℓ,r$$$\ell, r$$$ (1≤ℓ≤r≤n$$$1 \le \ell \le r \le n$$$) are given, which are the boundaries of the next query.
